voice.note: edge-tts 5.0.0+ removed custom SSML. Use the --rate/--volume/--pitch flags only, never SSML tags.

pacing.note: sentenceGapMs is silence inserted between sentences inside a scene. It is what lets a 38s narration fill a 55s scene without the delivery sounding rushed, and it gives the visuals room to land.

scenes.title: Title
sentences: SMARTWORK 360.
A smart task and performance management system for government offices, built as a module on the e-Office platform.
This is a working prototype.
Everything you are about to see is running live.
scenes.notes: Logo settles, wordmark fades, 'Working prototype · Live' chip appears last.

scenes.title: The problem
sentences: Government offices today have no single online tool to set goals, benchmark success, and measure productivity at three levels — the organisation, the team, and the individual.
Work is tracked on paper and through follow-up calls.
SMARTWORK 360 closes that gap.
scenes.notes: The three levels highlight in sequence, timed to the words organisation / team / individual in sentence 1.

scenes.title: Login and Parichay
sentences: Officers sign in with their government email, or through Parichay single sign-on.
Parichay is shown here in sandbox mode, since live integration requires onboarding by the National Informatics Centre.
Every user lands on a dashboard shaped by their role.
scenes.notes: login page -> Parichay sandbox screen (hold on the Sandbox mode pill) -> back -> employee chip -> /e/dashboard.

scenes.title: Employee — individual level
sentences: This is the individual level.
An employee sees only their own work — what is assigned, what is due today, what is overdue, and their on-time record for the month.
Opening a task shows its full history: who assigned it, the deadline, and every update made so far.
The employee records progress with a short note.
That update is saved immediately, and it is also written to the system's audit trail, which we will come to shortly.
scenes.notes: Kavita Joshi. KPI row -> Today's Focus -> /e/tasks -> open task drawer -> timeline -> type update -> slider -> Submit -> Audit chain (N blocks) grows.

scenes.title: Employee assistant and performance
sentences: Each employee has an assistant that answers from their live data, not from a manual.
Asking about pending work returns the actual task list.
The performance page shows the employee's own trend — tasks completed on time, and average time taken.
This is how the system measures productivity at the individual level.
scenes.notes: Click the hardcoded saffron Hinglish chip 'mere pending kaam kitne hain?'. Hold on the 'intent: my_pending_tasks' label. Then /e/performance.

scenes.title: Manager — team level
sentences: At the team level, a manager sees the whole section at once.
SLA compliance shows how much work is finishing within its deadline.
The morale indicator reads the tone of written updates using a language model, giving an early signal that a team is under strain.
The burnout list identifies who is overloaded, with a suggested action.
Work moves through the board by dragging a card, and every movement is recorded.
Submitted work arrives in a review queue, where the manager approves it or sends it back with a note.
scenes.notes: Anil Kulkarni (PWD) — NOT the Sunita Deshmukh login chip, Ramesh Patel lives in PWD. SLA ring -> morale gauge -> burnout list -> /m/burnout suggested action -> /m/board drag Pending->In Progress -> /m/reviews.
scenes.accuracyFlag: Sentence 3 says 'using a language model'. Your README states the shipped morale method is a word/lexicon scorer that BEAT DistilBERT (87.5% vs 85.0%), and the model footer on this very card can read 'Lexicon (offline mode)'. See video/README.md — suggested replacement wording is there.

scenes.title: Manager analytics
sentences: The analytics view answers the questions a supervising officer actually asks.
How much work is the section completing each week.
Which priorities are taking longest.
Where deadlines are being missed.
And whether workload and team morale are moving together.
scenes.notes: Four charts, each scaled 1.15x in turn as its sentence lands: Weekly throughput / Avg cycle time by priority / SLA breaches by week / Sentiment vs task load. Recharts entry animations need ~1.8s to settle first.

scenes.title: Admin — organisation level
sentences: At the organisation level, the administrator compares departments side by side — open work, overdue work, deadline compliance, and staff wellbeing.
The heat map shows where delays cluster, week by week.
Departments and users are managed from a single screen, with roles that control exactly what each person can see.
scenes.notes: Rajesh Iyer. Wait for the SECOND data wave — Morale and At-risk columns populate after the per-department fan-out, and recording early shows 0.00. Then heat map, then /a/directory.

scenes.title: Fraud and risk
sentences: The system also watches for irregular activity.
An anomaly detection model flags unusual patterns — a burst of status changes at two in the morning, work approved by the same person who submitted it, or a task marked complete in four minutes.
Each alert opens with the underlying evidence, so an officer can judge it themselves.
The system raises the flag.
A human makes the decision.
scenes.notes: Precision card -> anomaly scatter (night cluster) -> open the Vikas Meena self-approval row -> evidence panel, reason tags, raw JSON. Hold 1.5s on the evidence. Last two sentences land on a still frame of the evidence panel.

scenes.title: The audit trail
sentences: Every action in SMARTWORK 360 is recorded as a linked block.
Each block carries a fingerprint of the block before it, using the same cryptographic method as a blockchain.
Verifying the chain confirms that no past record has been altered.
Now we will attempt to alter one old record directly in the database, bypassing the application entirely.
The chain is checked again.
The tampering is detected, and the exact block where the record was changed is identified.
This is what tamper-evident means.
Records cannot be quietly edited after the fact.
Restoring the original data returns the chain to a verified state.
scenes.notes: THE SHOWPIECE. verify (green, hold 2s) -> cut to terminal card (demo:tamper) -> back to app -> verify (red, hold 2s, block number scaled 1.15x) -> Show block #N in the ledger -> terminal card (demo:reset) -> verify (green, hold 2s). The page refetches every 30s and will flip red on its own — the recorder pauses that route so the button press is what causes the flip on camera.

scenes.title: Guided tours
sentences: Staff training is often the hardest part of introducing a new system.
Every role has a built-in guided tour that teaches by doing — the user performs the real action to move forward.
It runs in English and in Hindi, and it can be restarted at any time.
scenes.notes: The one scene that deliberately lets the welcome modal appear. Start 2-min tour -> step through 2 steps -> land on the action step showing 'Try it yourself to continue' -> toggle हि on the card -> Skip tour.

scenes.title: Support assistant and self-repair
sentences: When something goes wrong, the officer does not need to raise a ticket.
Here, creating a critical task fails.
The assistant reads the error, explains the cause in plain language — a missing deadline rule for that department — and offers to correct it.
The correction is applied, and the task now saves.
That repair is itself recorded on the audit trail.
And there is one thing the assistant will never do.
Asked to repair a broken audit chain, it refuses.
A broken chain is evidence, not a fault.
The system can heal itself, but it cannot touch the record.
scenes.notes: MUST be recorded as ADMIN — the department field in the New task modal only renders for role ADMIN. Health + Critical has no SLA policy in the seed, so the 400 is genuine. Error banner -> Ask Saarthi about this -> attached error chip 'POST /tasks · 400 · SLA_POLICY_MISSING' -> Apply fix -> green 'Recorded on the audit chain as block #N' -> retry the task, it saves -> then type 'fix the broken audit chain' -> refusal.

scenes.title: Access, language and mobile
sentences: The interface is available in English and Hindi, and follows the accessibility standards set out in the Guidelines for Indian Government Websites.
It installs on a phone as an application, so field staff can update their work from where they are.
scenes.notes: Toggle हिंदी on /a/overview, then navigate one page in Hindi. Then a 390x844 mobile viewport of /e/dashboard. See video/README.md — the app has no in-app install button and no beforeinstallprompt handler, so this shows the installable manifest and the phone layout, not a click-to-install.

scenes.title: How it is built
sentences: The system is built on open-source technology, which keeps licensing cost at zero.
A web application, a documented interface layer with over forty endpoints, a standard database, and a separate service for the analytical models.
It can be deployed on NIC Cloud or any government-approved environment.
scenes.notes: Layers fade in as they are named: browser -> API -> database -> ML service. Your repo documents 66 endpoints; 'over forty' is deliberately conservative and stays true.

scenes.title: Close
sentences: SMARTWORK 360 brings goal setting, tracking and measurement into one place, at all three levels, with a record that cannot be quietly changed.
It is running today, and we would welcome the opportunity to demonstrate it in your office.
Thank you.
scenes.notes: Logo, live URL, GitHub URL, 'Prototype running today'.
